Story: As a developer, I can read assets from both clubs' ScorePlay platforms with our own API keys.
Acceptance criteria: Lists 20+ assets per club with metadata; keys kept in environment variables, not in code.

Story: As a developer, I can query the pre-indexed TwelveLabs index for both game broadcasts.
Acceptance criteria: Search returns time-stamped moments from the Spurs game and Tottenham vs Man United.

Story: As the rules engine, I receive every ScorePlay asset in one standard format.
Acceptance criteria: Maps league, club, type, source (broadcast, team photo, press conference, published edit, fan upload), length, game end time and rights partner; missing fields lead to Review, never Allow.

Story: As a media producer, I see which rostered players appear in an asset.
Acceptance criteria: Players matched from the provided rosters and headshots; opponents listed separately; spot-check of 10 assets is correct.

Story: As a partnerships manager, I see which partner logos and rival brands appear in an asset.
Acceptance criteria: Detects the provided partner logos (front of shirt, sleeve, major sponsors); flags whether the shirt sponsor is visible; flags brands on the rival list.

Story: As a producer, I'm told when broadcaster graphics are visible.
Acceptance criteria: Score bug or broadcaster graphics detected on broadcast clips and passed to rule N-07.

Story: As a compliance reviewer, I'm told about unidentified people and likely children.
Acceptance criteria: Counts unknown people and flags likely minors; never tries to name a fan.

Story: As a compliance reviewer, every asset gets a verdict for 7 uses in 3 regions.
Acceptance criteria: Loads rules.json; strictest verdict wins; time limits become a usable-until date and turn to Block when passed; uses no rule covers default to Review; the 4 sample assets reproduce the published test results.

Story: As a reviewer, I can read why each verdict was given.
Acceptance criteria: Each cell lists its reasons, most decisive first, with rule IDs; optional AI summary paragraph never contradicts the grid.

Story: As a club media team, I see the verdict on the asset inside ScorePlay.
Acceptance criteria: Verdict, reasons and usable-until date are saved on the asset and visible in ScorePlay after refresh.

Story: As a producer, I open one asset and see its passport.
Acceptance criteria: Shows preview, 7x3 grid with text labels (not color alone), reasons and usable-until date; loads in under 3 seconds.

Story: As a producer, I can scan the whole library by status.
Acceptance criteria: List with overall status per asset; filters for club, use, region, verdict and expiring soon.

Story: As a social media manager, I can ask what I can post in plain words.
Acceptance criteria: "What can I post on TikTok in the UK this week?" returns the matching assets, consistent with their grids.

Story: As the club's legal team, I can change a rule without a developer.
Acceptance criteria: Editing a value (e.g. 60s to 45s) and re-running updates verdicts on screen; shown live in the demo.

Story: As a producer, I'm warned before content expires.
Acceptance criteria: List of assets that expire in the next 7 days, with the uses affected.

Story: As a partnerships manager, I see how long each sponsor logo was on screen.
Acceptance criteria: Seconds on screen per partner logo for each video.

Story: As a fan at a watch party, I upload photos with a consent tap.
Acceptance criteria: Upload via the real-time path; fan consent and guardian consent stored with the asset; no consent means Block.

Story: As the club, I get only cleared fan photos in my library.
Acceptance criteria: Live check shows the grid within seconds; cleared photos go to the club library tagged 'fan content - consent on file' with the fan credited; rival-logo and child-without-consent cases are blocked with reasons.

Story: As a venue running a watch party, my screens only show content cleared for public display.
Acceptance criteria: Venue profile records official status and presenting sponsor category; playlist includes only venue-cleared assets; sponsor conflicts are blocked.

Story: As a producer, I can reuse published edits safely.
Acceptance criteria: Allowed on the platform it was published on; Review for any other platform.

Story: As the team, we have a demo set covering every verdict.
Acceptance criteria: 20-30 assets per club plus 10 fan photos, including rival logo, child, no-consent and over-length cases.

Story: As presenters, we can run the 3-minute demo even if the network fails.
Acceptance criteria: Rehearsed script; backup screenshots and screen recording of each step.

Story: As judges, we know the rules are samples.
Acceptance criteria: 'Sample rules - not legal advice' shown in the app and on slides; verdicts described as recommendations a person confirms.

Story: As judges, we understand the business case.
Acceptance criteria: Slides: problem, demo, business model (clubs, sponsors, venues), roadmap.

Story: As a fan, I give photo consent inside WhatsApp.
Acceptance criteria: WhatsApp Flows collects fan and guardian consent and links it to the upload.

Story: As a venue, I message my guests from my own WhatsApp Business number.
Acceptance criteria: Venue onboarding through WhatsApp Embedded Signup v4.

Story: As a venue or vendor, I plan watch-party programming in irl.group.
Acceptance criteria: Programming calendar, capacity, RSVP list, vendor slots and sponsor rules per venue.

Story: As irl.group, we can reach every ScorePlay club.
Acceptance criteria: Application to the ScorePlay Connect partner program submitted.

Story: As a club, the engine uses my real rules.
Acceptance criteria: Sample rules replaced with the clubs' rule sheets and reviewed by their legal teams.

Story: As a compliance lead, I can see who overrode a verdict and why.
Acceptance criteria: Audit log of every override with person, time and reason.

Story: Privacy
Acceptance criteria: Never identify fans by face; only flag 'unknown person'.

Story: Human in the loop
Acceptance criteria: Verdicts are recommendations; a person confirms any Review or override.

Story: Safe default
Acceptance criteria: Anything unknown or not covered by a rule is Review, never Allow.

Story: Speed
Acceptance criteria: A single-asset check completes in a few seconds during the live demo.

Story: Both clubs
Acceptance criteria: Every feature works for the Spurs (NBA) and Tottenham (Premier League) data.

Story: Accessibility
Acceptance criteria: Verdicts shown with text labels, not color alone.

Story: Secrets
Acceptance criteria: API keys never committed to code or shown on screen.
